Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking this through — attaching our first-pass capacity profile and a sample prompt set. High level context: Olive Apps is rolling an LLM inference tier into our production chat and summarization flows (customer support + internal knowledge worker assistant). We're exploring Redwood Dedicated for predictable latency and data isolation.

Quick answers from our intake form (attached worksheet has numbers by route):
- Peak concurrent sessions (web chat + API): 220 concurrent sessions (observed during M-F 10:00-12:00 PT)
- Average session pattern: short multi-turn chat (3.4 messages/session), median session duration ~75s
- Token mix (per request): prompt ~110 tokens median, response ~540 tokens median (we see a heavy tail; 95th percentile response length ~1,800 tokens)
- Request arrival shape: bursty (10–18x within 5–10 minute windows), esp. Monday mornings and after marketing blasts
- Required latency SLO: p95 <= 450ms for standard chat, p95 <= 900ms acceptable for long responses (summaries)
- Streaming: web chat uses streaming for user-visible responses; API calls are mostly synchronous with client-side timeouts of 10s
- Caching: permitted for system prompts and prompt prefixes, not for user-provided content
- Compliance: we need SOC2-type controls; interested in VPC/private deployment options and KMS integration
- Retention: logs/telemetry kept 30 days, training data never retained

Questions at our end: what fleet mix would you recommend for this profile (H100 vs A100 vs mixed), and what's your guidance for quantization/packing if we want to trade cost vs latency? Also please confirm likely autoscaling behaviour for these bursts.

Attachments: olive_capacity_profile_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), sample_prompts_and_templates.txt

—Sara

Sara — thanks, this is a great starting point and the spreadsheet helps a lot. A few clarifying questions so our pre-sales sizing isn't based on assumptions:

1) Burst shape: when you say 10–18x within 5–10 minutes, is that relative to a baseline of ~220 concurrents or is the 220 your observed peak after bursts? Can you share a short CSV with per-minute concurrency for the last 30 days?
2) 95th percentile response at 1,800 tokens — is that dominated by document summarization jobs (single long responses) or multi-turn worst-case chat?
3) For streaming: do you require guaranteed chunk-by-chunk token push (low-latency streaming) or is chunked polling acceptable?
4) Can you indicate the percentage of requests that are latency-sensitive (interactive chat) vs batch/summarization? Even 60/40 split materially changes fleet mix.
5) Any constraints on network egress costs or pinned regions?

Internally I'm looping in Marissa and Karthik to run a quick sizing sketch once we get the per-minute sample. Expect a short follow-up with an estimated GPU mix (capacity/oversubscription assumptions), suggested quantization, and burst autoscaling plan.

I'll block a 45-minute technical workshop next week (draft invite below) — if you can share the CSV ahead of the call that will let us run a quick sim.

On Fri, Oct 16, 2027 at 02:12 PM, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai wrote:
> FYI — forwarding Sara's intake (attached CSV). Key signals: baseline ~220 concurrents, 65% interactive, 35% long summaries, 10–18x marketing bursts, and streaming required for web chat.

Quick sizing sketch (conservative):
- Workload split: interactive (p50 req tokens ~110+280 resp = ~390 tokens) vs summarization (p50 ~110+540 = ~650 tokens) based on their sample set. Use median/95th from CSV for final sim.
- Throughput assumptions: we assume H100 provides ~1.8x throughput vs A100 for the model family they referenced (decoder+long-context). For streaming interactive, latency-sensitive tail is best served on H100-like machines.
- Fleet mix recommendation: start with mixed fleet: 60% H100 (interactive pools), 40% A100 (long-run summarization + batchable jobs).
- Oversubscription: interactive pools: conservatively 4.5x session oversub (continuous KV caching for system prefixes, batching disabled for low-latency paths). Summarization pools: 10x oversub with packing and larger batch windows.
- Quantization: int8 recommended for A100 summarization nodes (cost win, little p95 impact). For H100 interactive nodes, prefer fp16 or mixed-precision; int8 may increase jitter on streaming p95. Evaluate int8-fast kernels in a short perf benchmark during the workshop.
- Warm buffer: keep ~15–20% of peak interactive capacity warm to cover marketing bursts (based on 10–18x bursts; buffer reduces fallback risk). Autoscale cold-start for new pods ~45–120s depending on image/weights cache; we recommend regional warm capacity to keep user-visible latency within SLOs.

Cost note (very rough): for a sustained baseline of 220 concurrents with the above mix and oversub assumptions, ballpark committed fleet cost (monthly) in Dedicated reserved capacity terms: $85k–$140k/month depending on commits/term/quantization. We'll tighten this after running the CSV through our sim.

Deliverables before the workshop:
- A short spreadsheet with per-minute sim (I started one): https://drive.google.com/sim/oliveapps-sizing-sim (placeholder)
- A checklist of config knobs to validate during workshop: model family & sequence length cap, streaming chunk size, KV cache ttl, per-route batching window, warm buffer policy.

Karthik — can you run the CSV through the cluster sim and add a p50/p95 latency projection? I can pull the cost calc together.

—Marissa
